questions.question: Which of the following parts of the human body contains gustatory receptors?

__
 
• **The gustatory receptors which detect taste are present in the tongue.**
 
• **Gustatory receptors**
 
 
• **It is present on the tongue and is spread evenly across the taste buds.**
 
• **Their main function is to provide a sense of taste.**
 
• Gustatory receptors are found in the tongue.
 
• The gustatory system is much easier than the olfactory system.
 
• **Four primary taste varieties are generally recognized as sweet, sour, salty, and bitter.**
 
• In different regions on the tongue are present different sensitivities to the four taste varieties.
 
• The** tip of the tongue is the most sensitive to sweetness and saltiness.**

• It is present on the surface of the olfactory neurons.
 
• **Their main function is to sense smell.**
 
• These receptors equip sperm cells for finding the egg through a sense of smell.
 
 
 
• **Sensory receptors **occur in specialized organs such as the eyes, ears, nose, and mouth, as well as internal organs.

questions.question: Which of the following is the indigestible portion of our diet essential to the health of the digestive system?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Roughage.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Roughage is the indigestible portion of our diet essential to the health of the digestive system.
 
• Roughage is also known as fibre.
 
• Dietary fibre or roughage is the portion of plant-derived food that cannot be completely broken down by human digestive enzymes.
 
• Roughage is the portion of plant foods, such as whole grains, nuts, seeds, legumes, fruits, and vegetables, that your body can’t digest.
 
• Food rich in roughage may not help in providing nutrients.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Carbohydrates** are one of the essential nutrients in the human diet.

 
 
• There are two types of carbohydrates that can be digested by the human digestive system: sugar and starch.
 
 

 
• Proteins are essential nutrients for the human body.

 
 
• They are one of the building blocks of body tissue and can also serve as a fuel source.
 
 
 
• **Fat** is a nutrient, and your body requires it for energy, vitamin absorption, and heart and brain health protection, much like protein and carbohydrates.
 
 
• The backbone of a fat molecule is made up of glycerol, and the tails are made up of three fatty acids.

questions.question: Which one of the following is a rare disease caused by the deficiency of Vitamin D that causes the bones to become soft and to bend?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Rickets.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rickets is a childhood disorder of the bones where the bones become soft and prone to fractures. Bones tend to become weak due to an inadequate supply of nutrients, Vitamin D3 in particular.**
 
• It is also caused due to a** lack of calcium and phosphate** in the body. Weak bones can lead to bone deformities. Vitamin D largely comes from exposing the skin to sunlight.
 
• Other good sources of Vitamin D are fatty fish (such as tuna and salmon) and egg yolks.
 
• **Rickets** is a disease associated with the deficiency of **Vitamin D**.
 
• Rickets is of the following types:
 
 
• **Nutritional Rickets** -
 
 
• This is caused due to intake of food which lacks calcium, phosphorous, and vitamin D.
 
 
 
• **Hypophosphatemic Rickets-**
 
 
• It is caused due to low levels of phosphate. It is an X-linked genetic disorder where the kidneys are not able to control the amount of phosphate excreted in the urine.
 
 
 
• **Renal Rickets-**
 
 
• People suffering from kidney disorders have renal rickets. They are unable to regulate the amount of calcium and phosphate excreted in the urine.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pernicious Anemia:**

 
 
• It is a decrease in red blood cells that occurs when the intestines cannot properly absorb vitamin B1.
 
• Vitamin B12 is also referred to as cobalamin because it contains a metal ion. Cyanocobalamin is used in vitamin supplements and pharmaceuticals.
 
• Symptoms of Vitamin B12 deficiency are the smoothness of the tongue, gastrointestinal disturbances, nervous symptoms.
 
 
 
• **Lupus:**
 
 
• It is caused by the lack of immunity in the body.

questions.question: Which of the following body parts is directly affected by the disease called ‘trachoma’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Eyes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Trachoma**__

 __
 
• **It is a bacterial infection that affects your eyes. Hence, Option 1 is correct.**
 
• It is caused by the bacterium Chlamydia trachomatis.
 
• **Trachoma is contagious, spreading through contact with the eyes, eyelids, and nose or throat secretions of infected people.**
 
• It can also be passed on by handling infected items, such as handkerchiefs.
 
• **At first, trachoma may cause mild itching and irritation of your eyes and eyelids. Then you may notice swollen eyelids and pus draining from the eyes. Untreated trachoma can lead to blindness.**
 
• Trachoma is the leading preventable cause of blindness worldwide.
 
• Most trachoma cases occur in poor areas of Africa, where 85% of people with active disease reside.
 
• In areas where trachoma is prevalent, infection rates among children under 5 can be 60% or more.
 
• Early treatment may help prevent trachoma complications.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The four most common eye conditions leading to loss of vision or blindness are:
 
 
• Cataracts.
 
• Diabetic retinopathy.
 
• Glaucoma.
 
• Age-related macular degeneration.

questions.question: Which of the following diseases is caused by a virus transmitted primarily by Aedes mosquitoes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Zika fever.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Zika fever is caused by a virus transmitted primarily by Aedes mosquitoes.

 
• Zika virus is primarily transmitted by the bite of an infected mosquito from the Aedes genus, mainly Aedes aegypti, in tropical and subtropical regions.
 
 
• Aedes mosquitoes usually bite during the day, peaking during early morning and late afternoon/evening.
 
• This is the same mosquito that transmits dengue, chikungunya and yellow fever.
 
 
 
• The incubation period (the time from exposure to symptoms) of Zika virus disease is estimated to be 3–14 days.
 
• The majority of people infected with Zika virus do not develop symptoms.
 
 
• Symptoms are generally mild including fever, rash, conjunctivitis, muscle and joint pain, malaise, and headache, and usually last for 2–7 days.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tularemia **is a bacterial disease in humans, wild, and domestic animals.
 
• **Malaria** is a parasitic disease spread by mosquitoes. Humans are infected with the parasite after being bitten by infected mosquitoes.
 
• **Minamata disease **is a disease of the central nervous system, a poisoning caused by long-term consumption, in large amounts, of fish and shellfish from Minamata Bay.
 
 
• The causative agent is** methylmercury.**

questions.question: What is the dominant substance that makes up the hair, nails and the top layer of skin in the human body ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Keratin.**__

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• Human nails and hairs are made up of **Keratin.**
 
• **Keratinocytes** produce keratin, a type of protein that forms the basic component of hair, skin, and nails. 
 
• Keratin in the skin's outer layer helps create a protective barrier.
 
• Keratin is a type of protein that forms the cells that make up the tissue in nails, hairs, and other parts of the body.
 
• It makes hair strong and resilient.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Laminin** functions as a sticky glue, which holds cells and ECM together.

 
 
• It has active domains for collagen binding, cell adhesion, heparin-binding, and neurite outgrowth fragment.
 
• It modulates cell growth, motility, and signaling pathways.
 
• Cell types used are epithelial cells, endothelial cells, muscle cells, schwannoma, and hepatocytes.
 
 
 
• **Collagen** is the most abundant protein in mammals.
 
 
• In cell culture, it is used to study the growth, differentiation, and migration of cells. 
 
• Collagen Type I is used for fibroblasts or endothelial cells.
 
• Collagen Type II may be used for Chondrocytes and epithelial cells.
 
 
 
• 
 **Fibronectin** is a multifunctional protein involved in cell adhesion and spreading.

 
 
• 
 It also regulates cellular morphology, cell migration, cytoskeletal organization, hemostasis, and wound repair.
 
 
• 
 For cell types such as epithelial cells, mesenchymal cells, neuronal cells, fibroblasts cells, and endothelial cells you may use fibronectin.

questions.question: People who wear bifocal lenses have _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**presbyopia.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The gradual loss of your eyes' capacity to focus on** adjacent things **is known as presbyopia.
 
• It commonly appears in your **early to mid-40s** and worsens until you reach the **age of 65.**
 
• Presbyopia is caused by the** ciliary muscles weakening** and the eye lens becoming less flexible with age. As a result, the **eye's accommodation power** is lost, and the user is unable to view nearer objects well.
 
• **Glasses with bifocal power** and appropriate **focal lengths** are frequently used to remedy this problem. The **upper half** of the lens is** concave,** which corrects **myopia** and allows you to **see distant objects **clearly, while the** lower part** is** convex,** which corrects** hypermetropia** and allows you to see **nearer items** clearly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Hypermetropia**__** **

 __
 
• A person with **hypermetropia/hyperopia,** also known as **long sight,** can** see objects clearly from afar** but not up close.
 
• When the** eye is shorter than normal** or the** cornea is overly flat**, light rays **focus behind the retina**, causing hypermetropia (long-sightedness). The retina cannot concentrate light rays from close objects, such as book pages, clearly.
 
• It is **corrected **by spectacles or contact lenses with lenses that are** 'plus' or convex in shape.**
 
 
 
• **​Myopia__**
 __
 
• ​**Nearsightedness (myopia)** is a vision problem in which** items close** to you are **clearly seen** but objects further away are **blurry.**
 
• When light rays bend (refract) wrongly due to the structure of your eye,** focusing images in front of your retina** instead of on your retina.
 
• When one spends too much time in a **state of near focus**, myopia worsens. Activities like **reading **for extended periods of time or **knitting** might aggravate the issue.
 
• Myopia glasses commonly have a** concave (inwardly curved) lens**, which shifts the light's focus to help you see well. Myopia is corrected by **single vision lenses.**
 
 
 
• **​Cataract__**
 
 
• ​Cataract occurs when the normal lens of your eye becomes** hazy. Proteins** in your lens degrade, making objects appear **fuzzy, foggy, or less colourful.**
 
• The** most common** cause is** ageing.** This is due to the regular ageing of the eyes, which begins around the **age of 40.**
 
• **Other causes** of cataracts include someone having** cataracts in your family members**, having certain **medical problems** like diabetes, smoking, having had an **eye injury**,** eye surgery,** or** radiation treatments** on your upper body, having spent a lot of time in the** sun**, especially without sunglasses that protect your eyes from** damaging ultraviolet (UV) rays**, or using certain medications, such as** corticosteroids, **which may cause the early formation of cataracts.
 
• **Cataract surgery** is the only **effective treatment** for cataracts.

questions.question: In which of the following parts of the human body is the masseter muscle located?

__
 
• The strongest muscle (based on its weight) of the body is the masseter muscle which is located in the jaw__.
 
• The muscle masseter is a facial muscle that plays a major role in the chewing of solid foods.
 
• It is a facial muscle that plays a major role in the chewing of solid foods.
 
• The muscle has a parallelogram-like shape, binding to the mandible (lower jawbone) and the cheekbone.
 
• The muscle's function during the entire muscle's bilateral contraction is to lift the mandible and raise the lower jaw.

questions.question: Which part of the digestive system receives secretions from the liver and the pancreas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Small Intestines.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Small Intestine of the digestive system receives secretions from the liver and the pancreas.
 
• **The Small Intestine:**
 
 
• It is highly coiled and is about 6-8 meters long. It receives secretions from the liver and the pancreas.
 
• The digested food can now pass into the blood vessels in the wall of the intestine. This process is called **absorption**.
 
• The inner walls of the small intestine have thousands of finger-like outgrowths.
 
• These are called **villi.** (It increases the surface area of absorption of the digested food).
 
• The small intestine receives bile juice and stores it in the gall bladder.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] 

**Additional Information__**

 
• **Large intestine:**

 
 
• It is wider and shorter than the small intestine.
 
• It is about 1.5 meters in length.
 
• Its function is to absorb water and some salts from the undigested food material.
 
 
 
• **Gallbladder:**
 
 
• The gallbladder is a pear-shaped organ under the liver.
 
• It stores bile, a fluid made by the liver to digest fat.
 
• It breaks down fats into fatty acids, which can be taken into the body by the digestive tract.
 
 
 
• **The stomach:**
 
 
• It is a muscular hollow organ.
 
• It takes in food from the oesophagus (gullet or food pipe), mixes it, breaks it down, and then passes it on to the small intestine in small portions.
 
• The stomach stores the food for 4-5 hours.
 
• The food mixes thoroughly with the acidic gastric juice of the stomach by the churning movements of its muscular wall and is called the chyme.
 
• Gastric juice is made up of digestive enzymes, hydrochloric acid, and other substances that are important for absorbing nutrients - about 3 to 4 litres of gastric juice are produced per day.
 
• The hydrochloric acid in the gastric juice breaks down the food and the digestive enzymes split up the proteins.
 
• The acidic gastric juice also kills bacteria.

questions.question: _______ is the field of study concentrated on pregnancy, childbirth and the postpartum period.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Obstetrics.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• **Obstetrics **is the field of study concentrated on pregnancy, childbirth and the postpartum period.
 
• Ophthalmology is a branch of medicine and surgery which deals with the diagnosis and treatment of eye disorders.
 
• Oncology is the branch of medicine that researches, identifies and treats cancer.
 
• **Orthopedics**, also called orthopedic surgery, medical specialty concerned with the preservation and restoration of function of the skeletal system and its associated structures, i.e., spinal and other bones, joints, and muscles.

questions.question: Which of the following vitamins is also called 'cyanocobalamin'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vitamin B-12**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The mineral cobalt** is present in **cyanocobalamin (commonly known as Vitamin B12)**, which is a very complex, important vitamin.
 
• This vitamin, which is produced naturally by bacteria, is required for DNA synthesis and the creation of cellular energy.
 
• The cyano-, methyl-, deoxyadenosyl-, and hydroxy-cobalamin forms of vitamin B12 are among the many available.
 
• In supplements and pharmaceutical medications, the cyano form is the most common.
 
• Cyanocobalamin is available in a variety of pharmacological formulations, including tablets, injections, and nasal sprays.
 
• **Vitamin B12 (cobalamin) is a water-soluble vitamin** that aids in metabolism. It's one of the B vitamins, which are made up of eight different types. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Thiamine, often known as thiamin or vitamin B1**, is an important element that the body cannot produce. It's a dietary supplement or drug that's found in food and commercially synthesised.
 
• **Vitamin B6** (chemical name**- Pyridoxine-**4,5-Bis(hydroxymethyl)-2-methylpyridin-3-ol**)** is an essential ingredient because it is one of the B vitamins. The term "vitamers" refers to a collection of six chemically related molecules that can be interconverted in biological systems.
 
• **Niacin, **commonly known as nicotinic acid, is an organic molecule and a type of **vitamin B3** that is necessary for human health. 
 
• Vitamin B12 aids in the formation of DNA and red blood cells. Pernicious anaemia is a type of anaemia that makes it difficult for the human body to absorb vitamin B12.
